description: We’re DuneTech, a team of curious and motivated students taking on the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026! we’re excited to learn, collaborate, and turn ideas into a creative, practical solution using real NASA space data.
summary: Outpost Odyssey puts kids aged 7 to 12 in charge of a deep-space habitat on the Moon or Mars, turning real NASA mission logistics into a hands-on survival game. Most space materials for young learners stick to flat facts or feel way too technical, leaving kids out of the actual tough calls astronauts have to make every day. In our game, nothing is free. If a solar storm hits, players might have to pull power away from oxygen scrubbers or greenhouse crops just to keep their radiation shields running. We built the simulation around real NASA open datasets—tracking actual space weather spikes and harsh surface conditions—so every dilemma reflects genuine engineering constraints rather than made-up rules. By letting players test strategies, fail safely, and see how a small choice early on snowballs days later, Outpost Odyssey helps kids build real systems-thinking skills while learning what it truly takes to survive off-world.
details:
Outpost Odyssey is a lunar-based survival and mission-control simulator. Across a multi-sol mission timeline, players manage core habitat systems: Power, Life Support (Oxygen & Food), and Radiation Shielding.

Each turn presents players with realistic operational scenarios and environmental events, such as incoming solar flares, micrometeorite showers, or equipment maintenance needs. Instead of offering a "safe" or zero-cost answer, every decision forces a tangible trade-off. For example, running a high-energy scientific experiment yields mission points but drains battery reserves needed for overnight heating and hydroponic food production. Similarly, locking down the habitat to block radiation keeps crew health stable while temporarily halting external communications and solar array efficiency, allowing players to learn directly from scenarios.
